bertholomus's two-Spark Beam-1.0-501B-A23B recipe v0.2.0, its default TensorFold lane (beam-1.0-2x-dgx-spark bdfa59fa, tf/; MIT): tensor parallel 2 over the RoCE link, rank 0 serving the OpenAI API, with Reflection's DFlash2 drafter on both ranks. Engine: bertholomus/TensorFold, branch beam-1.0-tp2, at the REV of tf/beam-tf.env (d00201b4, TensorFold 0.6.6 with the beam family), installed on the stock nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3 image the creator runs (the creator publishes no image); the engine's CUDA extensions are built for the GPU present before each rank starts, as tf/beam-tf-build.sh does. Weights: bertholomus/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-EXL3-3bpw-2xGB10 at fb04dd69 (routed experts 3 bits, attention and dense MLPs 6 bits, about 90 GiB per node) and reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2 at 163b276b. Every served setting is the creator's (tf/beam-tf.env): 4-bit drafter weights and draft head, 5 drafts a step adapting between 3 and 5, 16 rows a decode step, the mma3 prompt expert kernel, 4,096-token prompt chunks split in 1,024-row pieces, 4 prompt cache entries, reduce-scatter prompt sums, 4 NCCL channels, the glibc malloc thresholds, 4 sequences decoding together and --context 1,048,576 (Beam's longest, asked). The engine sizes its fp8 KV pool at each start from what a 9 GiB MemAvailable floor leaves, up to that context: the creator's served start held 868,352 positions per node, so the API facts state 868,352 tokens; that is the creator's measurement, not a floor, and the pool can come out larger or smaller on nodes with more or less free memory. Reasoning is always on (Beam always writes its analysis channel); reasoning_effort picks minimal to max (max when unset); tool calls with tool_choice auto, as Beam's harmony format; no structured output (xgrammar is not installed). Deviation from the creator: the image applies one patch to the engine (adapters/beam/bertholomus-tensorfold-tp2/patches/0001-tool-parameters-integral-number-for-integer.patch). Beam's chat template types a JSON-schema integer as number, so the model writes 17.0 and TensorFold's decode_parameter returned the text, a JSON string; on hardware the shared product case returned {"left":"17.0","product":"323.0","right":"19.0"} with a correct answer. With the patch an integral number for an integer parameter comes back as the integer (17); an upstream PR to bertholomus/TensorFold follows once hardware confirms. Not ported: the creator's API key file, 127.0.0.1 listen address, memguard.sh and MIN_START_GIB preflight (platform concerns); the Controller supplies NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME, NCCL_IB_HCA and NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX (the creator's GID 5 is its own nodes'). Memory: each peak is 130,663,231,488 bytes minus the creator's lowest MemAvailable (10,740 MiB head, 11,089 MiB worker) minus the 4,063,231,488-byte idle host use admission charges: 115.34 GB on the entrypoint and 114.97 GB on the worker, estimates until tried here; selected weights per rank (96.9 GB of target plus the 3.9 GB drafter) plus 8 GB overhead are about 108.7 GB, so the load is predicted to fit with the pool taking the rest. Upstream figures (30.6 tok/s decode on ~2K prose, 45.5 tok/s on ~2K code, 64.7 tok/s aggregate over 4 code streams, about 1,400 tok/s cold prefill, KL 0.0121 and 96.87% top-1 agreement against BF16) are the creator's claims, not measured here. The repository's vLLM lane (gb10/, 655,360 tokens) is a different engine and not this recipe. Licences are information only: recipe scripts MIT, TensorFold and the Beam weights Apache-2.0.

display.description: Unpruned GLM-5.2 (744B total, 40B active; QuantTrio Int4-Int8Mix, compressed-tensors) on four Sparks with vLLM tensor parallel 4 over the native multi-node launcher, a 200,000-token context, FP8 DeepSeek-MLA KV in a fixed 10.95 GB pool, MTP with four drafted tokens, FLASHMLA_SPARSE attention with the Triton sparse-MLA kernels and b12x, and full CUDA graphs. Basis: tonyd2wild's recipe (Apache-2.0; kernels from CosmicRaisins/glm-5.2-gb10, mods from ciprianveg, decode-aware scheduler by penguinchang, all Apache-2.0) on drowzeys' published probe-modded vLLM ab666069 image, which carries the same tag name upstream builds locally; upstream's run-time kernel bind mounts are copied into the image at build time. Related recipes for this model and Spark count: glm-5-2-quanttrio-vllm-four (drowzeys kit) and the same creator's NVFP4-KV variant. Upstream figures (32.5 tok/s mean, 36 peak single stream) are claims until measured here. Memory follows the creator's settings: gpu-memory-utilization 0.91 beside the fixed 10.95 GB FP8 KV pool and a 200,000-token context, as in tonyd2wild's launch.sh at 162d7a76 (lines 208 and 209); with a fixed pool the utilization is vLLM's startup free-memory check, and upstream rejects 0.90 explicitly (README line 367). Upstream runs with 0.6 to 0.9 GB of MemAvailable and 3.6 to 4.5 GB of swap in steady state (README lines 342-345). The declared peak is the per-rank loading floor: the weights, the pool and 8 GB of runtime overhead; the reserve is 8 GB, and admission keeps the platform memory floor free beside the peak.

display.description: Full GLM-5.3 (744B MoE) on six DGX Sparks with KindlingAI's gr8, a from-scratch CUDA inference engine (no vLLM, PyTorch or NCCL at serve time), at tensor parallel 6 over the ConnectX fabric (a 200G RoCE switch). The weights are KindlingAI's exlr8 release v0.6 at its bit325 width profile (about 3.25 bits a routed weight). The KV cache is pure FP8 (native 656-byte MLA latent rows, no INT4 quantisation, BF16 kv_b projections) with a 1,507,328-token pool, requests up to 1,048,576 tokens, eight at once and zero-copy shared prefix pages, uncapped exact MoE routing (KL 0 against the uncapped engine, the creator's figure), DFlash2 plus MTP=2 drafting and the creator's tuned v1.2.0 prefill and decode settings, with the QO cache written on the first boot and read by later ones. The recipe runs gr8's published v1.2.0 image (commit ab2eb95f) with the settings of kindlingai/recipes at 13c24ac4 (glm-5.3/dgx-spark/6x/exlr8-fp8kv-gr8) and a placement wrapper that reads the platform's VONK_* environment and uses the release in place from the read-only model mounts; the DFlash2 drafter is converted for each rank on its first start. Options: the creator's uncapped-exact, balanced or fast MoE preset (MOE_UNION_CAP 0, 48 or 32); DFlash2 or MTP only; the creator's K4 quality profile (bit390, a 524,288-token pool, 10.4+ GiB free a box by its figure); the creator's optional 200 GB persistent SSD KV store. The creator's lowest free memory a box was 6.41 GiB under its 972K-token stress, below the platform's usual 8 GiB margin, so it is tried on idle Sparks first. About 659 GB of model files a box. Each box mounts the width files its manifest reads whole, where the creator's launcher range-fetches only the box's part from Hugging Face. Thinking is always on in GLM 5.3's template: a request that turns thinking off is accepted: gr8 thinks at the lowest effort and withholds the reasoning, and a small max_tokens can end inside the thinking. Licences, for information: the weights are under Z.AI's GLM-5.3 License (KindlingAI's exlr8 additions also CC BY 4.0), the engine and the recipe MIT; IncoAI's DFlash2 drafter is Apache-2.0.
display.title: GLM 5.3 EXLR8 FP8 KV gr8 six Sparks

display.description: GLM-5.3-Flash on two DGX Sparks with TensorFold's native Zig/CUDA server (TensorFold 1.3.0, upstream 81de26f6 plus MiaAI-Lab's 16 engine patches), one rank per Spark over the ConnectX-7 link with RoCE all-gathers that use both PCIe links of the cabled QSFP port when the platform's fabric setup passes both RoCE devices (the engine takes up to two from NCCL_IB_HCA). Serves MiaAI-Lab's EXL3 4 bpw TensorFold checkpoint (EXL3 routed experts, BF16 elsewhere; Mia-AiLab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-4bpw-TensorFold at the revision the kit pins) with the kit's served settings: a 1,048,576-token window, 8 concurrent requests sharing an FP8 KV pool of 512-row pages, 8-bit dense and head weights, DFlash2 drafts at 4 bits, image input (up to 50 images a request; the default image has no video runtime), tool calling and structured outputs, a default reply budget of 32,768 tokens, thinking off by default with reasoning effort Max when a request turns it on, and earlier turns' reasoning dropped from the prompt. Based on MiaAI-Lab's GLM-5.3-Flash DGX Sparks kit 1104 at commit a691916c (Apache-2.0), which supersedes her earlier two-Spark TensorFold kit; the creator publishes no image of it, so the recipe builds her Dockerfile (CUDA 13.3.1, Zig 0.17.0, sm_121) with her patches vendored, with a baseline-CPU Zig target because the image is built on a hosted arm64 runner, and without her optional video runtime. The kit's single-stream and aggregate rates, prefill rates and memory figures are upstream claims, not measured here; per Spark the kit's README names about 83.3 GiB of model, 12.5 GiB of KV pool, 3.6 GiB of prompt cache and a 9.5 GiB reserve kept free as its measured served configuration. The recipe keeps that 9.5 GiB reserve rather than the kit's newer 6.5 GiB: the creator calls the 6.5 GiB and 5 GiB pair predicted and not measured yet, and a 6.5 GiB reserve would leave MemAvailable under the platform memory guard's 8 GiB threshold. Licences, for information: the quantization is Apache-2.0 per the kit's NOTICE, with Z.AI's MIT licence kept for the base model; the DFlash2 drafter is Apache-2.0 and is not used with the MTP drafter option. Thinking is chosen per request: a request can set reasoning_effort or chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking, and reasoning comes back in reasoning_content.

display.description: Single-DGX-Spark vLLM TP1 + MTP3 profile for the 99 GiB Mia mirror of the local-inference-lab Qwen3.8 Flash Next NVFP4 checkpoint (text, image and video). The 27 GiB PLE table is served from a memory-mapped packed file built once into the platform cache, so it stays evictable page cache. The adapter bakes MiaAI-Lab's PLE offload, MXFP8, QSA FP8-KV, reduced-vocabulary MTP drafting and block-drop patches into the pinned arm64 image. Defaults follow upstream: 262144 context, FP8 KV, BF16 recurrent state, MTP 3, four sequences, 2048-token prefill chunks; contexts up to 524288 use YaRN. GPU memory utilisation 0.786 follows the current upstream .env.sample budget for KV_TARGET_GIB=20, HOST_RESERVE_GIB=26, and a 121.69 GiB host (95.60 GiB budget); it is derived from that owning profile, not a measured constant. The README's 0.780 (94.87 GiB) table documents an earlier KV_TARGET_GIB=16, five-sequence profile. Upstream claims (not measured here): 48.7 tok/s single stream; 162.9 tok/s aggregate needs 8 streams (upstream ran max-num-seqs 8 with a 28 GiB reserve, this recipe defaults to 4). GB10 memory correction: Per-node peak budgets utilization × 130,663,231,488-byte unified memory plus at least 8 GB for CUDA context/graphs, FlashInfer workspace, auxiliary heads and CPU/mmap buffers; 8 GB reserve, with a separate 6 GB OS floor. This is a conservative budget, not a measured footprint.

Upstream image defaults: 4,096 context, 32 sequences, 0.70 memory utilization (raise the context setting for longer windows; not validated upstream). The upstream registry image is not public, so the runtime is rebuilt from upstream's Dockerfile steps on the public laguna-m1 image digest that its mutable :latest base pointed to. Licences: Apache-2.0 for the model and package per the HF card and Dockerfile label (information only). Performance figures are upstream claims. GB10 memory correction: Per-node peak budgets utilization × 130,663,231,488-byte unified memory plus at least 8 GB for CUDA context/graphs, FlashInfer workspace, auxiliary heads and CPU/mmap buffers; 8 GB reserve, with a separate 6 GB OS floor. This is a conservative budget, not a measured footprint.

display.description: Full GLM-5.3 (744B MoE) on six DGX Sparks with KindlingAI's gr8, a from-scratch CUDA inference engine (no vLLM, PyTorch or NCCL at serve time), at tensor parallel 6 over the ConnectX fabric (a 200G RoCE switch). The weights are KindlingAI's exlr8 release v0.6 at its bit325 width profile (about 3.25 bits a routed weight). The KV cache is pure FP8 (native 656-byte MLA latent rows, no INT4 quantisation, BF16 kv_b projections) with a 1,507,328-token pool, requests up to 1,048,576 tokens, eight at once and zero-copy shared prefix pages, uncapped exact MoE routing (KL 0 against the uncapped engine, the creator's figure), DFlash2 plus MTP=2 drafting and the creator's tuned v1.2.0 prefill and decode settings, with the QO cache written on the first boot and read by later ones. The recipe runs gr8's published v1.2.0 image (commit ab2eb95f) with the settings of kindlingai/recipes at 13c24ac4 (glm-5.3/dgx-spark/6x/exlr8-fp8kv-gr8) and a placement wrapper that reads the platform's VONK_* environment and uses the release in place from the read-only model mounts; the DFlash2 drafter is converted for each rank on its first start. Options: the creator's uncapped-exact, balanced or fast MoE preset (MOE_UNION_CAP 0, 48 or 32); DFlash2 or MTP only; the creator's K4 quality profile (bit390, a 524,288-token pool, 10.4+ GiB free a box by its figure); the creator's optional 200 GB persistent SSD KV store. The creator's lowest free memory a box was 6.41 GiB under its 972K-token stress, below the platform's usual 8 GiB margin, so it is tried on idle Sparks first. About 659 GB of model files a box. Each box mounts the width files its manifest reads whole, where the creator's launcher range-fetches only the box's part from Hugging Face. Thinking is always on in GLM 5.3's template: a request that turns thinking off is accepted: gr8 thinks at the lowest effort and withholds the reasoning, and a small max_tokens can end inside the thinking. Licences, for information: the weights are under Z.AI's GLM-5.3 License (KindlingAI's exlr8 additions also CC BY 4.0), the engine and the recipe MIT; IncoAI's DFlash2 drafter is Apache-2.0.
display.title: GLM 5.3 EXLR8 FP8 KV gr8 six Sparks
